items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: His buddy, Mr. Tarleton... told my father that I could get a job there

ctx.x: I alone went to this place which happened to be a factory that manufactured ropes. I was hired and worked half a day and never went back for my pay. The place was so dusty with the dropout of rope dust that it was difficult to breathe.

A few days later my father found out where I was and came to take me home. He was working in a cleaning and pressing shop, pressing mens' suits and certain kinds of women's dresses and coats and he lived in a two-roomed apartment in the back of the shop. This shop was owned by Mr. Thompson, the man whose horn I used to clean and polish, and Mr. Will Tarleton, who was a very good friend of my father. He had also played cornet in the Centerville band and he was a great collector of Bert Williams records. This shop…

I had been with my father and brother Ulysses about 2 days when my father noticed a lot of little bugs in the bed. He knew what they were but I didn't, and he knew that I was the one who had brought them there. I had been away from home 4 or 5 months and had not had a bath during all that time, so I was full of lice. My father burned my underclothes and socks and bought me a new suit. Naturally I had to take a bath as hot as I could stand it.
